title: Location
description:
A place in a data centre, addressed the way an operator addresses it: site, room, row, rack, rack unit. Kept as its own entity rather than fields on Resource because many resources share one location, and because a location exists before anything is installed in it -- a rack position in a floor plan is a real thing to plan against.

Addressing INSIDE a chassis is not here. That is Redfish PartLocation on the Resource, because it is relative to a parent rather than to the building.

site.description: Site code as the business uses it, not a street address. This is the field that appears in a ticket subject line.

row.description: Row label as painted on the floor or containment.

rack.description: Rack label as printed on the rack. For an NVL72 this is the unit an entire validation campaign is scoped to, which is why it is a first-class field rather than a label.

rack_unit.description: Lowest rack unit occupied, counting from the bottom, matching how racks are physically numbered and how NetBox stores position. Fractional for half-U placements.

rack_face.description: Which side the resource is mounted on. Two resources may share a rack unit if they are on opposite faces, and a validation that ignores face will report a phantom collision.

grid_reference.description: Floor tile or grid square, where the facility uses one. This is what a crane plan and a cooling survey are drawn against.

coordinates.description: Position within the room, for floor plans and cooling models. Room-relative metres rather than lat/long, because building-relative is what every facility drawing uses.

power_zone.description: Facility power zone or feed identifier. Present because 'which racks lose power together' is a question about the building, not about the racks, and it cannot be derived from anything else here.

cooling_zone.description: Facility cooling zone, typically the CDU or manifold group serving this position.
